title: Consistent spinner overlay and label behavior for button loading/disabled states
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Standardize how the Button component shows progress and disabled states across variants (primary/secondary/tertiary/icon-only) and themes. Deliver a token-driven spinner layout that avoids layout shift, preserves focus order, communicates state to assistive tech, and remains theme-aware (dark/high-contrast). This replaces several ad-hoc patterns that caused visual regressions during last release and inconsistent behavior between icon-only and label buttons.
acceptance_criteria: Buttons show an inline overlay spinner without layout shift for all size variants
Icon-only buttons display a centered spinner and maintain a visible hit target and accessible name
When loading, visible label either shows microcopy (e.g., 'Saving...') or remains visually present per variant rules; screen readers receive an appropriate aria-live update
Focus order and keyboard activation remain consistent while a button is loading/disabled
Spinner and spacing use design tokens (spinner-size, spinner-gap, button-spinner-opacity) and respect reduced-motion and high-contrast settings
No new regressions in button hover/active/focus visual states across themes (light/dark/high-contrast)
Automated visual snapshot tests and accessibility checks (axe/voiceover) pass for new behavior
tasks: Design: produce token spec for spinner size and gap (xs/sm/md/lg) and token mapping for each button size
Design: create visual comps for Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, and Icon-only with loading overlay and inline label variants
Engineering: implement CSS+React changes to support overlay spinner and token usage
Engineering: add aria-live announcements and ensure icon-only buttons surface accessible names
QA: regression test existing button interactions and run visual diffs across themes
Docs: update component doc with migration notes and examples for legacy consumers
decisions: Use an overlay spinner that sits on top of the button content (semi-transparent layer) to prevent layout shift across different label lengths
Maintain the visible label for non-icon buttons when loading but switch copy to developer-provided 'loadingLabel' if supplied; otherwise fall back to original label with aria-live announcement
For icon-only buttons, replace icon with spinner but keep aria-label present and expose loading state via aria-busy=true on the button
Spinner sizing and gap values will come from new tokens so runtime can map to quantized CSS values for consistent pixel snapping
tradeoffs: Overlay prevents layout shift but increases CSS complexity and requires z-index discipline across nested containers
Keeping the visible label reduces surprise for users but may conflict with compact UI requirements; offering 'loadingLabel' provides opt-in succinct messaging
Replacing the icon in icon-only buttons is visually clean but requires careful attention to hit target and screen reader names to avoid regressions
